_meta.note: Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026. Broker notes read in full: PL (1-Aug-2026, 20-May-2026), BOB Capital (1-Aug-2026), ICICI Securities (20-May-2026). Others from dated secondary listings.

industry.capacity: India refining capacity 258.1 MMTPA (FY26), throughput 272.1 MMT; IOC group 80.75 MMTPA (~31%), going to ~98 MMTPA by FY28.
industry.demand: Petroleum product consumption +2% in FY26 (diesel +4%, petrol +6%); in Q1FY27 petrol +7% and diesel +5% QoQ, ATF -5%, LPG -20% (commercial supply curbs).
industry.pricing: Petrol and diesel prices are formally deregulated but in practice set by the three PSU OMCs with the government's consent; prices were held for long stretches, including through the 2026 Gulf war. Household LPG is sold below cost and losses are compensated by the government case by case: in Oct-2025 MoPNG approved ₹14,486 cr for IOC for under-recoveries up to Mar-2026, paid in 12 monthly instalments from Nov-2025.
industry.war2026: US-Iran conflict from end-Feb 2026: Strait of Hormuz traffic disrupted, Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG under force majeure. Indian basket US$63.87 (Q3FY26) -> US$83.01 (Q4FY26) -> US$100.74/bbl (Q1FY27). Government cut SAED on petrol and diesel by ₹10/litre on 27-Mar-2026 and re-imposed export duties on diesel and ATF; retail prices raised in tranches from May-2026 (~₹3/litre each at first, ~₹7.5 on diesel cumulatively per the Q1 call). A 60-day US-Iran truce from mid-June eased prices before renewed escalation.
industry.src: ar26 MD&A; q4call; q1call; businesstoday.in (27-Mar-2026); ICICI Securities (20-May-2026)

competition: BPCL and HPCL are the other two state OMCs (both refiners with large retail networks; HPCL relies most on bought-in product); Reliance (Jamnagar) and Nayara (Vadinar) are private refiners with smaller retail networks; MRPL (ONGC group) and CPCL (IOC group) are standalone refiners. IOC has the largest refining capacity (~31% of India), the largest pipeline network and ~42% of domestic petroleum sales (ar26).

excluded.HINDPETRO: Earnings distorted on 30-Sep-2026: HPCL has the highest marketing-to-refining ratio of the three OMCs, so the Q1FY27 marketing loss collapsed its trailing earnings; trailing EV/EBITDA 11.9x (five-year median 5.7x) and P/E 44.6x are not a re-rating. Shown with HPCL as a sensitivity row.

peers.note: IOC itself is excluded from its sector move. The natural set leaves three usable names (BPCL, MRPL, CPCL), the minimum under the thin-peer-set rule; the widened oil & gas set is shown as a sensitivity. Sector move measured on EV/EBITDA (our primary method), the EV/EBITDA analogue of the house P/E factor (pharma precedent, PLAYBOOK §7c).

street._note: Standing on 30-Sep-2026. Fundamental targets only. Post-Q1 notes (1-Aug-2026): PL, Motilal Oswal, BOB Capital. Pre-Q1 notes (May-2026) still standing as far as public sources show: ICICI Securities, Geojit, Nomura, UBS.

brokers.thesis: Upgrade from Reduce: core GRM US$19.1/bbl in Q1 despite peak SAED; LPG under-recovery narrowing; government support expected. GRM US$10.0/6.5, GMM ₹1.5/4.7 per litre FY27E/28E.
Q1 beat driven by >₹150bn of marketing inventory gains; capex cycle nearing its end; risks: LPG under-recoveries, borrowings ₹1.4 lakh cr, SAED changes.
Volume growth and expansions positive, but retail margins challenged by elevated crude; TP cut from ₹173; major benefit of capex only after FY29.

street.methodView: The street values IOC on EV/EBITDA of consolidated EBITDA (4.5-5.5x, on Dec-27E to FY28E) plus investments at or near market (Motilal Oswal, BOB Capital, ICICI Securities), or on P/B (PL 0.8x FY28E). We follow the EV/EBITDA sum of the parts and show P/E and DCF as cross-checks.

ownership.history: Government 51.5% unchanged; ONGC and Oil India (both government-controlled) a further 19.4% ('Government' category 19.57%). FIIs 7.5% (Jun-25) -> 9.8% (Mar-26) -> 9.1% (Jun-26).

governance.board: Chairman A.S. Sahney (previously head of IOC's petrochemicals vertical); Director (Finance) Anuj Jain. As a Maharatna CPSE, IOC's board is appointed by the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas; the statutory auditors are appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General (C&AG), who also comments on the accounts (AR FY26 carries a revised auditor's report after C&AG comments).
governance.independentDirectors: No independent directors on the board: the Audit Committee was discontinued from 28-Mar-2026 and the Q1FY27 results were approved by the full board.
governance.pricing: Retail petrol, diesel and LPG prices are set in consultation with the government; minority shareholders bear under-recoveries until (and unless) compensated.
governance.relatedParty: Large purchases from JVs (Petronet LNG ₹11,414 cr of products in FY26) approved by shareholders as material related-party transactions.

moat: Scale and infrastructure: ~31% of India's refining capacity, >20,000 km of pipelines (the cheapest way to move crude and products inland), 43,000+ fuel stations, 46% of LPG and 54% of ATF. These lower costs but do not protect margins: prices are administered, the product is a commodity and the government decides when OMCs absorb losses.
critiques: Marketing margins are a policy variable: in 2022 and 2026 the government held prices while crude spiked, wiping out a year's marketing profit.
Inventory gains flatter Q1FY27 (~₹15,000 cr finished goods); without them the quarter was a large loss.
